newsitem.title: USA: Carson Pirie July same-store sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Carson Pirie July same-store sales rise.

text.p: Carson Pirie Scott & Co said Thursday that same store sales for the four weeks ended August 2, 1997 rose 7.9 percent from the same period a year ago while total sales for the 1997 period increased 10.9 percent from last year to $67.4 million.
For the 1997 second quarter same store sales were up 5.5 percent from a year ago and total sales increased 8.3 percent to $243.8 million, the retailer said in a news release.
For the year-to-date, same store sales rose 4.7 percent and total sales advanced 8.7 percent to $501.9 million.

Stanton Bluestone, chairman and chief executive officer, said he was pleased with July sales results. "We achieved solid sales gains in nearly all merchandise categories and we recorded double digit comparable store sales increases in Feminine Apparel, Men's Apparel, Home Textiles and Shoes," he said in a statement.

Looking ahead to the balance of the year, he said, "I am hopeful that the sales momentum that we achieved in the first half of 1997 will carry over into the second half. General economic conditions should remain favorable for the balance of 1997 and I believe that both our inventory content and proven business strategies position Carson to take advantage of opportunities as they arise."
Carson Pirie Scott operates 52 department stores and four furniture stores.
